title: Feedback
body:
**Feedback** is the system's response confirming that an action registered and telling the user
what happened. Its absence produces the repeated click, because a user with no confirmation
reasonably assumes the action was lost.

The deadlines come from [[Human Capabilities]], and engineering convenience has no say in
them:

```
within 0.1 s     feels instantaneous, so no explicit feedback is needed
within 1 s       the user's flow of thought survives, though a delay is noticed
beyond 10 s      attention is lost, so a progress indicator is required
```

A progress bar that shows real progress serves better than a spinner, because it answers how
long as well as whether. An operation that cannot report real progress at least reports that it
is alive.

Feedback also has to be specific about the outcome. "Error" tells the user something failed and
nothing about what to do; naming what went wrong and what would fix it is the difference
between a message and a dead end. The same applies to success, since a form that submits with
no visible change leaves the user unsure whether to submit again.

In [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]] this is where [[Asynchronous JS]] becomes an
interface problem: a [[Fetch]] takes hundreds of milliseconds and the interface has to say so,
since the user cannot see the network.
